proposed_widenings.name: modify_roll_reroll
proposed_widenings.justification: The Luck property grants a free reroll of one failed D20 Test per dawn. No reroll effect atom exists in types.ts. The v4 taxonomy names modify_roll_reroll but it is absent from the TS surface. The existing modify_roll_advantage and modify_roll_numeric atoms do not cover rerolling a die after it has already been rolled and failed.
proposed_widenings.evidence: If the weapon is on your person, you can call on its luck (no action required) to reroll one failed D20 Test if you don't have the Incapacitated condition. You must use the second roll.

proposed_widenings.name: ItemDestructionPolicy — property_loss_on_empty variant
proposed_widenings.justification: The Wish charges being depleted causes only the Wish property to be lost, not the whole item. The current ItemDestructionPolicy discriminated union has none / last_charge_roll / permanent_on_empty, all of which apply to the entire item. A partial-property-loss variant is needed for items that shed individual charge-based abilities while retaining other mechanics.
proposed_widenings.evidence: The weapon loses this property if it has no charges.

notes: The passive +1 attack/damage/saves and the Wish charge-cast are fully encodable with existing surface atoms (passive PassiveMechanics + composite ActivatedAbilityMechanics with grant_spell_access charge_cast mode, ChargePoolResource with 1d3 initialCount, dawn reset). The primary blocker is the Luck property: a reroll of a failed D20 Test is mechanically distinct from advantage (which applies before the roll) and from numeric bonus modifiers. modify_roll_reroll exists in v4 taxonomy but is absent from types.ts. Because Luck is a primary named property and not a secondary rider, partial encoding would be misleading and is not attempted. The property-loss gap (Wish only, not full item destruction) is a secondary widening that would need to be addressed alongside the reroll atom.
